Would you rather lose your tactioception (sense of touch) or your propioception (kinesthetic sense)?

Losing your sense of touch results in more sever injuries because you cannot react to something you cannot feel and will not remove your body from danger. On the upside when you do inevitably hurt yourself terribly you wouldn't feel it. Other than that you would life a relatively normal life, and many do with this condition.

Losing your sense of spacial perception would result in losing all effective mobility. You would not be able to walk as you could not perceive the motion of your own legs and feet and how they relate to the ground. You would not be able to adapt to gravity, you would have no balance. You would not be able to feed yourself as you could not even know where your own mouth is in relation to your fork.

I'll take the former thanks.

Ah but sense of touch is different than feeling pain. They have different circuitry. If you put your hand on a stove burner while its on, you don't immediately feel pain but will instinctively move your hand away (unless you're retarded).
So it would simply result in things like over-gripping and heavy stepping, which I think would still be far less debilitating than full loss of mobility.

What is the cognitive error where a news story on a subject you actually have knowledge of is absurd, but you look at the next news story and believe it to be true?

A decade ago I really believed most anything I saw online that looked "reputable". These days I just assume that everything is either:

  • Advertising
  • Shilling
  • Misinformation
  • Propaganda
  • Possibly real news

If there are multiple sources that don't share the same agenda who report similar stories, then it might actually be factual. If it's a small local source, then it can feel more valid sometimes. Still plenty of shilling on MajorNewsNetworkLocalStation23.

Other than that, I really just assume everything is potentially a false flag. I work in the game industry and I can say fuck pretty much everything about news that relates to my industry. The major sites are mostly advertisers or agenda-pushers, so I just don't visit then them anymore.

However, the research side of news in the industry is impeccable. That part has a very limited exposure to people like us who want to actively read white papers and prototype/verify/discuss/improve upon the results. This is what I actively consider news because it is generally unfiltered and has a lot of back and forth on discussions of new techniques and how to make them applicable to film and game engines.

And then I lapped up the episodes on prostitution, drugs, gambling, counterfeiting, and human trafficking ( things I have no familiarity with ), wanting to take them at face value because it all seemed legit, but unable to fully accept them because of that first episode's slant.
